title: The Lipschitz image of an integer-weighted Lebesgue piece is an integer multiplicity current (supplied step 5, B3; Simon 6.3.5–3.9)
statement: Assume, as hypotheses, (CB) the frozen type of Submission.cmcdt_lp_covector_norm_bounds, (IMC) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, and (IMSc) the conclusion of the frozen type of Submission.cmcdt_im_series. (IMSc) says: for all P, k and W : ℕ → 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with Σ_l M(W_l) < ∞ there is S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with S(ω) = Σ_l W_l(ω) (HasSum) for every ω, M(S) ≤ Σ_l M(W_l) and spt S ⊆ closure ⋃_l spt W_l, and S is integer multiplicity if every W_l is. Let N', k ∈ ℕ, n := k + 1, L ≥ 0, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{N'} be L-Lipschitz, A ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, and g : ℝⁿ → ℤ measurable with ∫_A |g| dλ < ∞. Then there is an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{N'}) with S(ω) = ∫_A g(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_0, …, DH(u)e_{n−1}) du for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^{N'}), where DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u and e_a is the standard basis of ℝⁿ.
